identity.title: Luminous Infrared Galaxies with the Submillimeter Array. IV. <SUP>12</SUP>CO J = 6-5 Observations of VV 114

paper_type_evidence.quote: VV 114 was observed with ALMA during cycle 0 in $^{13}$CO $J$=1-0 (Saito et al. in prep.) using the compact configuration. We obtained calibrated $uv$-data from the ALMA archive.

evidence.quote: We model the molecular gas at the peak position of $^{12}$CO $J$=3-2 ($\alpha_{J2000}$ = 01$^{h}$07$^{m}$47.453$^{s}$, $\delta_{J2000}$ = -17$^{d}$30$^{m}$25.037$^{s}$) in VV 114E.
VV 114 (Arp 236, IC 1623, IRAS 01053-1746) is a nearby LIRG at a distance of 86 Mpc ($H_{o}$ = 70.5 km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, $\Omega_{M}$ = 0.27, $\Omega_{\Lambda}$ = 0.73; 1$''$ = 417 pc)

question.value: What are the beam-averaged physical conditions (Tkin, nH2, N_CO, 12CO/13CO abundance) and the CO-to-H2 conversion factor of the molecular gas in VV 114E, using new SMA 12CO J=6-5 plus low-J CO data including ALMA 13CO J=1-0?

evidence.quote: We use the radiative transfer code RADEX and a Bayesian likelihood code to constrain the temperature ($T_{\rm{kin}}$), density ($n_{\rm{H_{2}}}$) and column density ($N_{\rm{^{12}CO}}$) of the molecular gas.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA$\#$2011.0.00467.S.

bands.value: ALMA cycle 0 13CO J=1-0 (band not stated); SMA 690 GHz receiver for 12CO 6-5

evidence.quote: The $^{12}$CO $J$=6-5 emission in VV 114 was observed with the SMA on 2008 August 26 using a two-point mosaic.

evidence.quote: We recover the short spacings of the $^{12}$CO $J$=2-1 and $^{12}$CO $J$=3-2 SMA datasets using the JCMT datasets.

archive_products_used_as_is.value: Calibrated ALMA uv-data obtained from the archive

evidence.quote: We obtained calibrated $uv$-data from the ALMA archive.
The absolute flux scale was set using Uranus and checked using Callisto suggesting an accuracy level of the flux calibration of 20%.

masking.value: Integrated intensity map using channels with emission, 2 sigma cutoff

evidence.quote: We created an integrated intensity map with a 2$\sigma$ cutoff using velocity channels with emission from VV 114 (see Figure 1).

continuum_subtraction.value: uv continuum subtracted using line-free channels (ALMA data)

evidence.quote: The $uv$-data were continuum subtracted using line-free channels and a 40 km s$^{-1}$ cleaned datacube was created.

primary_beam_correction.value: all integrated intensity maps corrected for primary beam

evidence.quote: All integrated intensity maps were corrected for the primary beam.

smoothing.value: All maps degraded with Gaussian taper to 6.5 x 3.7 arcsec

evidence.quote: We applied a Gaussian taper to the observations to degrade the resolution.
The observations and calibration details are given in Paper I.
We use the the method of Paper III assuming the flux scales of both datasets to be the same.

unstated_but_needed: ALMA 13CO J=1-0 weighting/robust, cell size, clean threshold and beam details

Saito et al. in prep. for ALMA observation details

method.value: Degrade all maps to 6.5x3.7 arcsec via Gaussian taper, convert to K km/s, divide maps with 2 sigma cutoff

evidence.quote: We have degraded the resolution of all the maps to the resolution of the OVRO $^{12}$CO $J$=1-0 map, 6.5$''$ $\times$ 3.7$''$.

analysis_steps.goal: RADEX grid and Bayesian likelihood fit

method.value: RADEX grids in Tkin, nH2, N12CO with 13CO grids; Bayesian likelihood code fits 12CO and 13CO line fluxes

evidence.quote: The Bayesian likelihood code determines the most probable solutions for the physical conditions of the molecular gas by comparing the RADEX calculated and the observed $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO line fluxes.
We also generate a second $^{13}$CO grid expanding the relative abundance to $^{12}$CO (\[$^{12}$CO\]/\[$^{13}$CO\] = 10 – 10$^{5}$; Grid 2).

assumptions.value: Priors: column mass below dynamical mass, column length below region size, 0<tau<100

evidence.quote: The third prior constrains the optical depth to be 0 $<$ $\tau$ $<$ 100.

fitting.value: Likelihood with 1DMax and 4DMax; four parameters Tkin, nH2, N12CO, filling factor

evidence.quote: The likelihood code generates two calculated values for each parameter: the 1DMax and the 4DMax.
To see if hitting the upper limit of \[$^{12}$CO\]/\[$^{13}$CO\] affects our results, we use Grid 2 with the expanded range of values.

method.value: Mass from 4DMax column density and xCO divided by 12CO J=1-0 luminosity; dynamical-mass upper limit

evidence.quote: assuming a $^{12}$CO to H$_{2}$ abundance ratio of $x_{\rm{CO}}$ = 3 x 10$^{-4}$ (Ward et al. 2003), we can measure the CO-to-H$_{2}$ conversion factor

validation.value: Compared with Downes & Solomon 1998 and dynamical-mass upper limit

evidence.quote: The upper limit is consistent with the radiative transfer model-derived value for $\alpha_{CO}$.

used_for.value: Imaging and processing of SMA and ALMA uv-data

evidence.quote: The calibrated $uv$-data were converted to FITS format and then imported into CASA for further processing and imaging.
we use the radiative transfer code RADEX (van der Tak et al. 2007)
Data reduction was done with the IDL MIR package.
using the `Starlink` software (Currie et al. 2008)
This research made use of APLpy, an open-source plotting package for Python
The total flux of $^{12}$CO $J$=6-5 in the SMA map is 150 $\pm$ 40 Jy km s$^{-1}$.
The $^{12}$CO $J$=6-5 line is only detected in VV 114E (Figure 1 and 2).

claims.hypothesis: What are the gas conditions in VV 114E?
claims.experiment: RADEX plus Bayesian likelihood on CO SLED

evidence.quote: Grid 2 shows a maximum probable solution of a cold ($T_{\rm{kin}}$ = 38 K), moderately dense ($n_{\rm{H_{2}}}$ = 10$^{2.89}$ cm$^{-3}$) molecular gas component

claims.finding: About three times the local ISM value, explaining the high line ratio

evidence.quote: The most probable value of \[$^{12}$CO\]/\[$^{13}$CO\] in VV 114E is roughly three times larger than the value seen in the local interstellar medium

claims.hypothesis: Is alpha_CO consistent with the ULIRG value?

evidence.quote: This value agree within uncertainties with the value widely used for ULIRGs determined by Downes $\&$ Solomon (1998

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Grid 1 solution (hot 390 K, diffuse) rejected because abundance ratio hit grid upper limit

evidence.quote: The most probable \[$^{12}$CO\]/\[$^{13}$CO\] value hit the upper limit of our grid

limitations_admitted.value: Missing flux in 6-5 SMA map ~89%; no high-resolution short-spacing data

evidence.quote: we are missing 89 $\pm$ 10 $\%$ of the flux

referee_caveats_inferred: Beam-averaged single-position modelling with only 6 line fluxes for 4-5 parameters
Heterogeneous resolutions and missing flux in 6-5 may bias the SLED
ALMA data role minor and not described in detail
